text:
<@UA14TGLTC>
> I seriously wonder what mental model people have when they use AI especially right out of the box
I'd love to see a serious scientific study on this!

My mental model of basic LLMs (before agents etc.) is: they map language into a high-dimensional vector space and then do interpolation and extrapolation in that space. Meaning they capture what people have written, irrespectively of whether this writing represents reality or not. As long as you stay in domains for which most available writing represents reality, you can use it as a proxy for the real world, and get good answers from chatbots. This breaks down at the frontiers of human knowledge (scientific research), or for controversial topics (politics), or for topics that not much has been written about (my life). In those cases, you can still use LLMs as hypothesis generators, but not for knowledge retrieval.

I am pretty sure that my mental model is not typical for the AI-using population, if only because most people would stop reading my above paragraph at "high-dimensional vector space".

May virtual meetup • <https://time.is/1800_27_MAY_2026_in_UTC?Virtual_Meetup|Wed May 27 at 18:00 UTC> • <https://luma.com/15v0fpx1|RSVP>

I was always afraid this would happen. It's been — what — 20 years? Longer? Of waiting. Wondering. Ignoring.

Feeling too afraid to feel. Wanting it to be something. It not.

Well no longer!

This week, we'll have demos ~from at least two people. Yeah, that's right, we don't have a third person to demo something yet. I guess this is the quiet time of year. If you wanna demo something, DM me and say so! Would love to have you.~ TOO LATE SUCKERS! We're now _packed_ with demos. Everyone rules.

• Jasmine Otto has an update to a project she demoed before called Multiplayer Bitsy, which is a cute lil env for making games, used in education. This is legit authentic use stuff, y'all'll love it.
• Ivan Lugo reached out with a cool web-based IDE experiment he's been tinkering on.
• Luke Stanley has a… well, heck, I'm just gonna copy-paste what he said cuz it rules: "a 2D visual language topic map ZUI with a tricky no-overlap but high semantic spatial fidelity condition (from highly dimensional semantic embeddings). It's an annoyingly thorny problem that people will laugh at as being hard in no time at all though. (But that's probably true of most things.)"
Cool.
